The best European strikers this century - ranked by you

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.
  • There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.
  • This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The top 10 European strikers of the 21st century.

Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One.

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

Laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won substantial titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'.".

Recent findings suggest that honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player.".

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

Honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher.".

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries.".

Zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

Balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think.".

Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible.".

It has been revealed that honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that.".

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

According to recent reports, honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi.".

According to recent reports, balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent.".

Industry observers note that laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was.".

According to recent reports, what does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

According to recent reports, laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career.".

Balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him.".

Honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible.".

Sources indicate that there was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

In a recent development, balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others.".

According to recent reports, honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind.".

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him.".

Recent findings suggest that balague: "He noted he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter.".

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his.".

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

According to recent reports, honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being.".

Sources indicate that laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've said he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey.".

Sources indicate that runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

In a recent development, honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing.".

Sources indicate that laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

"There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever.".

Industry observers note that of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

According to recent reports, balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted.".

Recent findings suggest that laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think.".

Honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” by giving Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card against Liverpool, an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluded.
  • Yoro was given his marching orders when he hauled down Swedish striker Alexander Isak in the opening stages of last Sunday’s fiery match at Anfield.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” by giving Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card against Liverpool, an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluded.

Yoro was given his marching orders when he hauled down Swedish striker Alexander Isak in the opening stages of last Sunday’s fiery match at Anfield.

Debate raged over Isak’s touch and whether goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have collected the ball had Yoro not made contact.

Even referees’ chief Howard Webb concluded that the call was “certainly not clearly wrong”, but then Manchester United appealed to the Football Association for wrongful dismissal and successfully removed his one-match ban on Tuesday.

The three-person panel’s written reasons were published on Thursday and stated: “The commission members were unanimous that, taking the foul committed by LY (Yoro) out of the scenario, AI (Isak) would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

“Despite the fact that AI had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball – that control had, in effect, passed to the advancing MUFC goalkeeper who in the view of the commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before AI could get to it and shoot at goal.

“To the mind of the commission, the referee had made an ‘obvious error’ in deciding that AI (Isak) would have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity.”.

Industry observers note that webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, told the Match Officials: Mic’d Up programme which aired on Tuesday, shortly after confirmation the ban had been removed: “There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he (Isak) would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

Sources indicate that “I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”.

The FA’s independent panel, which was made up of former Blackburn and Middlesbrough winger Stuart Ripley, former Sheffield United and Notts County forward Tony Agana and ex-Walsall goalkeeper Mick Kearns, disagreed.

The reasons confirm that United submitted technical information to the panel which concluded Isak would have been, at best, 1.8 metres short of the ball even if Yoro had not made the challenge.

The reasons state that the commission “had no way of testing the validity of this analysis undertaken by the club and as such the evidence was viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly”.

To add to the confusion, the Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel is reported by the Daily Mail to have backed Barrott’s call and the decision of the VAR John Brooks not to recommend a review.

The five-person KMI Panel is comprised of three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative and one from Pro Ref, and its findings for the match week where the incident occurred are due to be published on December 2.

Pro Ref declined to comment on the Mail story, or on the commission’s findings. Manchester United have been approached for comment.

In a recent development, the reasons revealed that United also submitted a video of a challenge by Brighton’s Pascal Struijk on Wilson Isidor of Sunderland last month. Struijk was shown a red card after the VAR recommended a review for denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. Struijk’s suspension was removed after an appeal to the FA by Brighton.

The removal of the ban means Yoro is free to face Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday.

United encountered further refereeing controversy in their 2-2 Champions League draw away to Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday night.

According to recent reports, the Red Devils had a first-half goal disallowed after Polish referee Szymon Marciniak blew for what looked at best a very soft-looking foul by Youri Tielemans before Amad Diallo had put the ball in the net. They then had a winner ruled out when VAR recommended a review for what was deemed to be a foul by United’s Patrick Dorgu on Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, though the Brazilian appeared to have fumbled into his own net before the Dorgu challenge came in.

To rub salt into their wounds, Tielemans – who was booked for the challenge that led to the Diallo goal being disallowed – was then shown a second yellow in injury time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China Renaissance, a top dealmaker in the country’s tech industry, mentioned it would suspend trading of its shares and delay the release of its annual results because it still can’t get in touch with its founder.

Industry observers note that bao Fan, 52, started the boutique investment bank in 2005 and has been unreachable since the middle of February, according to the company. Shares in China Renaissance have plunged since Bao went missing, at one point dropping as much as 50%.

Recent findings suggest that china Renaissance remarked in late February that it had learned Bao was “cooperating in an investigation” being carried out by certain authorities in the country. It gave no other details.

Chinese media have reported Bao might be assisting in an investigation related to a former executive at China Renaissance.

In a filing on Sunday, China Renaissance mentioned auditors couldn’t complete their work or sign off on their report because of Bao’s absence. The board was also unable to give an estimate about when it would be able to approve its audited results for 2022 or dispatch its annual report by an April 30 deadline as required by Hong Kong’s listing rules.

Missing Chinese billionaire CEO assisting authorities in investigation, company claims.

Trading in the company’s shares was suspended from Monday as a result.

Bao is known as a veteran dealmaker who works closely with top technology companies in China. He helped broker the 2015 merger between two of the country’s leading food delivery services, Meituan and Dianping. Today, the combined organization’s “super app” platform is ubiquitous in China.

His team has also invested in US-listed Chinese electric vehicle makers Nio (NIO) and Li Auto and helped Chinese internet giants Baidu (BIDU) and JD.com (JD) complete their secondary listings in Hong Kong.

Industry observers note that over the weekend, China’s top anti-graft watchdog introduced an investigation into Liu Liange, former party secretary and chairman of Bank of China, according to a statement by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the State Supervision Commission. The bank is state-owned and one of the country’s four biggest lenders.

Liu is suspected of “serious violations of discipline and law,” the statement noted. He is among the most senior financial executives targeted in a broader financial crackdown by President Xi Jinping.

In January, Wang Bin, former party chief and chairman of China Life Insurance, was charged by national-level prosecutors with taking bribes and hiding overseas savings.

— Michelle Toh contributed reporting.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure that doomed 40 of its spacecraft went off without a hitch Tuesday morning (Nov. 24).

It has been revealed that an Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation lifted off at 6:14 a.m. EST (1114 GMT) from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), right at the end of the 29-minute window that opened at 6:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou).

The launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical glitch affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace.

Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit, will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which presently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft.

It has been revealed that amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur, suffered a problem shortly after launch.

Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' tech giant has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's Latest Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9.

It has been revealed that vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test.

Industry observers note that the Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure.

This morning's launch was the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following introduces in February, April and June of this year.

How Premier League's substantial six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'big six' clubs.
  • Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.
  • In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'big six' clubs.

Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.

In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.

The six biggest clubs - Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.

And the gap is growing. Every season.

BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the substantial six have exploded, examines new trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.

Recent findings suggest that companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it. It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.

In England, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.

Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham.

This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance issues.

Let's look at how the gap has grown.

We will use Everton, the only club not in the massive six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.

This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.

In a recent development, in 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the big-six average and Everton was Â£120m. In 2024-25, that gap had grown to Â£442m.

So what has driven this huge escalation?

In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.

"The major football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire stated.

"You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices.".

Only 10% of Everton's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the big six it is 45%.

It means Everton, and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income. It makes up 66% of their revenue.

For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.

It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.

This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.

But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.

When the European Super League proposal was torpedoed, Uefa created a upcoming financial deal called the value pillar.

This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or Â£713m, for the historically most successful clubs.

In a recent development, at the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned Â£37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool Â£35.5m and Chelsea Â£33.3m. Newcastle received only Â£13.6m.

The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.

According to recent reports, their value pillar is projected to be worth Â£25m this season. But that will still be less than the substantial six clubs in the competition.

The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.

Take a look at the financial trend of the significant six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.

In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the big six.

Sources indicate that not just by a small amount. They were Â£74m behind Tottenham, and Â£200m below Liverpool and Manchester City.

City's matchday income is the lowest, with the club's huge revenues largely due to commercial deals.

City, however, have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, inflating the value by using "sham contracts" with sponsors.

The club deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appealed against the verdict.

Chelsea's problem is simple - seats.

Sources indicate that stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion. The rest of the substantial six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.

Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of Â£80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal.

Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their significant six rivals, Chelsea's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.

"Matchday spend has become increasingly important," Maguire said. "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.

"As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast.".

Matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea, rising only Â£16m over the past 10 years. United's has grown by Â£69m and Spurs, thanks to their fresh ground, by Â£85m.

"Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire said. "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.

In a recent development, "Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League. Manchester United are a brand in their own right. And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial.".

Chelsea's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.

But there are signs that, financially at least, the big six could become the big five.

You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.

That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).

There is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players. PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.

"This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire remarked. "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the big six.

"SCR is different to PSR rather than better. For some people, change is advantageous. For others, it isn't.".

Industry observers note that the major six generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the other clubs. So they can spend hundreds of millions of pounds more on their squads.

This makes the big six even more powerful in the transfer market.

"Look at the clubs who voted against SCR - Brighton, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Leeds," Maguire said.

"It's very noticeable that those clubs have traditionally been very good at player sales, while they have tended to have lower matchday and commercial revenues.".

Most of the significant six - the outlier being Chelsea - are not remotely close to the Premier League's 85% SCR limit.

Sources indicate that if you give clubs more money to spend on transfers, the likelihood is they will do just that. And the numbers back that up.

Premier League clubs spent Â£3.5bn - not only a highest total for a summer window, but it almost smashed the record for a whole season, the Â£3.53bn set in 2025-26.

The annual accounting cost of previous transfers, or amortisation, has been rising year on year.

"Over the course of the last decade, transfer amortisation has more than doubled and close to tripled," Maguire said.

"Which means that on average, clubs in the Premier League are now spending, or now have a cost which goes into their SCR calculations of just under Â£100m.".

Uefa fears that SCR will make matters worse, and have an inflationary impact across Europe.

And you can see why it is concerned.

In the summer 13 Premier League clubs broke their transfer record.

Brentford, Brighton, Palace, Leeds and Nottingham Forest all spent more than Â£40m on a player - unthinkable until recently.

So we have learned that the substantial six have more money than ever, and the gap is so huge it is impossible for any other club to compete with them, financially at least.

And this is an important point: other than Villa and Newcastle, the other clubs are not trying to compete with the massive six.

Clubs like Brentford and Brighton have shown that smart models are just as effective as fat wallets.

They sign the potential stars of the future, nurture them and then sell them to the substantial six.

Football's ecosystem recycles the significant-six money through the transfer market.

But it is a precarious business for these other clubs.

"The smaller clubs have to get it right on a more regular basis than the bigger clubs," Maguire said.

"The big six can afford to make signings which are Â£60m and Â£70m, who turn out to be relative flops, and still have those players on high wages for several years.".

And this is perhaps the key point about the vast finances of the major six.

The commercial power of the big six does not guarantee success. After all, United sit in the relegation zone.

Yet Mauricio Pochettino, their fresh manager, may well get the chance to revamp the squad despite the club spending Â£945m on players in the past five years.

It has been revealed that the richest clubs can try to spend their way out of trouble. Again and again.

But the rest of the league are only a couple of bad transfer windows from catastrophe.

And that is the real gap between the big six and the rest.

  • Industry observers note that sometimes, the funniest thing you can do on the internet is fail spectacularly.
  • If you've spent any time scrolling through TikTok or Instagram Reels lately, you've probably heard his now-viral refrain: "Ahh, almost, almost." What began as a moment of frustration on Twitch has since become the internet's go-to response to everything from missed basketball shots to the everyday indignities of being alive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that monkey D. Luffy is once again at the scene of the internet's latest viral meme. Well, technically, it's Twitch streamer Jynxzi playing as the beloved One Piece protagonist in Fortnite, but the distinction hardly matters when you're watching the aspiring King of the Pirates repeatedly fail to obtain a pirate token.

Industry observers note that sometimes, the funniest thing you can do on the internet is fail spectacularly. Or, in Jynxzi's case, come agonizingly close to succeeding.

If you've spent any time scrolling through TikTok or Instagram Reels lately, you've probably heard his now-viral refrain: "Ahh, almost, almost." What began as a moment of frustration on Twitch has since become the internet's go-to response to everything from missed basketball shots to the everyday indignities of being alive.

Here's what you need to know about the "ahh almost almost" meme and how it escaped the confines of Twitch.

Sources indicate that the voice behind the meme belongs to Jynxzi, a popular Twitch streamer known for his animated reactions and exaggerated competitive spirit. With 11.8 million followers on Twitch, Jynxzi regularly streams games like Rainbow Six Siege, League of Legends, and Fortnite, often collaborating with other streamers like iShowSpeed and StableRonaldo.

According to recent reports, the meme appears to have originated from a Fortnite livestream in early November, during which Jynxzi repeatedly tried (and failed) to obtain an in-game pirate token. Adding to the comedic effect was his declaration that he was putting in the work while everyone else was out partying. Despite his apparent dedication, success continued to elude him.

Clips of the stream began circulating on TikTok in early November, and it didn't take long for the audio to take on a life of its own outside of the gaming community.

Industry observers note that at its most basic, the meme is a reaction to a near miss. But part of what makes it so funny is the gap between how much confidence and effort someone brings to a task and how little they have to show for it. Sometimes, the person in question isn't even remotely close to succeeding, which makes Jynxzi's insistence that he's "almost" there all the more amusing.

It has been revealed that one popular iteration of the trend pokes fun at hustle culture. Videos begin with someone ostensibly working toward a goal, accompanied by the caption "while they're out partying btw," before cutting to footage of them failing at the very thing they've been practicing.

On TikTok, students document their study sessions only to reveal their failing test grades, a skier attempts a jump and loses their skis in the process, and even a snow leopard fails to catch a mountain goat. In one particularly relatable example, a student sits down to study only to get distracted by K-pop fancams. (We've all been there. Or at least I have.).

Naturally, the meme has found a particularly receptive audience among sports fans. Even NBA teams like the Orlando Magic and the Denver Nuggets have gotten in on the joke.

Think of it as the antithesis of a motivational edit. Instead of rewarding all that hard work with a triumphant moment of personal achievement, the meme celebrates the much more relatable experience of falling short.

You don't necessarily need to know who Jynxzi is to appreciate the joke, either. Much like other bits of streamer vernacular that have made their way into the wider internet lexicon (hey, chat), "almost almost" works just as well as a standalone reaction.

Sometimes, the grind simply doesn't pay off. But at least the memes do.

From YouTubers and TikTok stars to streamers and podcasters, Mashable talks to creators about how they built their platforms, the gear they swear by, and the trends they see coming next.

Sources indicate that crystal Bell is the Digital Culture Editor at Mashable, where she leads coverage of the creator economy, internet culture, and digital life. Her work focuses on the people, platforms, and communities shaping modern entertainment, from YouTube creators and livestreamers to fandoms, social media trends, and the evolving relationship between technology and culture. She also oversees the Mashable 101, the publication's annual list recognizing the internet's most influential creators.

Previously, she was the entertainment director at MTV News, where she helped expand the brand's coverage of fan culture, K-pop, and the internet's most passionate communities. Her work has appeared in Teen Vogue, Rolling Stone, PAPER, NYLON, ELLE, Glamour, NME, W, The FADER, and elsewhere on the internet.

She's exceptionally fluent in fandom and will gladly make you a K-pop playlist and/or provide anime recommendations upon request. Crystal lives in New York City with her two black cats, Howl and Sophie.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Federal President’s latest major trip takes him to Africa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This blog is now closed. Read below for more on these stories and all other things Germany on Monday, November 23.

Thank you for following our coverage of headlines from Germany on Monday, November 24.

The Federal President’s latest major trip takes him to Africa. Frank-Walter Steinmeier has just visited the Ivory Coast and is continuing on to Ghana and Kenya. His goal: to encourage more German companies to invest in Africa.

Sources indicate that frank-Walter Steinmeier has visited 31 African countries during his political career. Even as foreign minister, he traveled regularly to the continent; as federal president, he has made twelve trips so far.

Sources indicate that from early on, he viewed Africa not only through the lens of development aid and humanitarian support, but also — much like former Chancellor Angela Merkel — as a market for the German economy that has been underutilized thus far. In 2015, as foreign minister in the Merkel administration, Steinmeier played a central role in the creation of the German-African Economic Summit.

Sources indicate that on his current trip as well, Steinmeier is advocating for greater German engagement in Africa. In Abidjan, the capital of the Ivory Coast, following a meeting with Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara, he called on German companies to step outside their comfort zone and take greater advantage of the opportunities offered by the country and the continent.

The Ivory Coast is considered a location with growing potential. Despite its proximity to the Sahel region, which is plagued by terrorism, the country is relatively stable politically. The economy is growing by about six percent annually. Germany has more intensive trade relations with the Ivory Coast than with any other country in sub-Saharan Africa, and nowhere else in sub-Saharan Africa do so many people learn German — an advantage for German small and medium-sized enterprises — all of which both presidents emphasized very clearly during their meeting in Abidjan.

Up next, Steinmeier is scheduled to visit Accra, Ghana, for the sixth German-African Economic Summit, where more than 600 business representatives are expected to attend. As the summit’s initiator, the Federal President will open the event together with the host, Ghanaian President John Mahama. He will be accompanied by a ten-member business delegation representing industry, the financial sector, and energy consulting.

The Economic Summit is taking place at a time when Germany’s relations with African countries are undergoing fundamental changes. In light of geopolitical shifts, Africa is increasingly coming into focus as an economic and trade partner.

Recent findings suggest that the continent’s share of German foreign trade presently stands at just under 2%, or around €30 billion. At the same time, German exports to Africa are rising by at least 6% annually. And since Germany’s economy aims to reduce its dependence on China in the future, opportunities in Africa are growing.

From Ghana, Frank-Walter Steinmeier will travel on to Kenya, the final stop on his tour of Africa.

Environment Minister Carsten Schneider on Monday vowed that Germany will continue to move away from burning fossil fuels despite the failure of the COP31 declaration in Antalya, Turkey, this weekend.

Speaking at an event in Potsdam, Schneider said: "We will clearly maintain our course on climate protection in Europe and Germany, but above all one that makes us independent of oil and gas because otherwise we are vulnerable to blackmail and our economic performance becomes extremely volatile.".

Schneider expressed disappointment less at the result of the two-week conference than its format, which he remarked was far more focussed on spectacle than substance.

It has been revealed that speaking of his vision for a format for future climate conferences, Schneider said: "Basically, I don't need so many people there. What I need are the relevant decision makers with whom I negotiate and make decisions.".

Although he voiced relief that the final document from the conference had not represented a step backwards — as well as stressing that some 30 countries had pledged to maintain the move away from fossil fuels — Schneider acknowledged that it had been nearly impossible to find consensus with Russia and Saudi Arabia at the table.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius urged calm over reports that Russia was planning to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space as early as next month.

"First of ​all, ‌let's remain calm, because there are reports — that's true — but ‌it's ​not clear what kind of weapons these are, and the ​effect they might have depends, in ⁠turn, ​on where they ​are deployed," Pistorius told ​reporters in ‌Berlin.

In a recent development, "Therefore, it's too early to ​speculate ⁠publicly about this. We are consulting ⁠internally ​and taking the necessary measures.".

German public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung first reported on the matter, which remarked that internal intelligence reports circulated among NATO countries earlier this month said that Russia was ready to bring the alleged satellite, named Sputnik-S, out of storage in Moscow.

The reports remarked Russia may be planning to launch it as soon as December.

Nuclear weapons are banned in orbit by the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, of which Moscow is a signatory.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated not allowing Ukraine intoNATO in 2008 was a mistake.

At the2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania, German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine.

US President George W. Bush mentioned he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO.

But both Germany and France mentioned that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance, but offered no timetable.

At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO.

To which Merz stated, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented.".

Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he said "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Russia to end its "dangerous provocations" after two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in Poland on Friday.

Merz delivered those remarks after having met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin on Monday.

"Poland can count on our full solidarity. And if necessary, NATO will of course defend every inch of allied territory," Merz noted.

Merz remarked Europe and NATO must strengthen their defenses.

Drones have repeatedly strayed into NATO airspace in the year since Russia released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The incident also came at a time as Poland was hosting a two-week military exercise by Ukraine's allies.

German startup investments in fields such as robotics and defense are set to almost triple this year, a study noted on Monday.

The German Start-up Association and the Joachim Herz Foundation study predicted that investments in so-called "deep tech startups" will surge from just €2.9 billion ($3.17 billion) last year to 8.1 billion ($8.9 billion) this year.

The study described the rise as a "major success for Germany as a business location.".

"Deep tech" typically refers to developing cutting-edge technologies based on scientific research, such as AI, biotechnology and quantum computing.

A handful of massive fundraising rounds by firms including humanoid robot developer Neura Robotics,  AI drone maker Helsing and defense tech group Quantum Systems drove the investment boom.

The study also highlighted about 300 newly introduced deep tech startups are expected to be founded this year, a 40% rise compared with last year.

Newly found startups tend to be founded around economic hubs like Berlin and Hamburg, which are also home to leading universities and research institutes.

The study also highlighted challenges, including limited funding compared with their US counterparts and insufficient support to move startups from the laboratory to the real world.

Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.

They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.

More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.

Similar reports have also emerged to the north of Germany, in Denmark.

As in Germany, Danish police noted they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools.".

Read more about the disruptive incidents that have targeted Europe in recent weeks.

Germany's Freie Wähler (Free Voters) party have chosen a fresh chairman, weeks after their former front man Hubert Aiwanger unexpectedly passed away on November 4.

In a recent development, the party revealed on Monday that Bavaria's Digital Affairs Fabian Mehring is to succeed Aiwanger both as party leader on the federal level and as one of two co-chairs of the Bavaria section of they party. The second state co-chair still needs to be decided.

Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel room at the age of 55 with no foul play suspected. He's been the party's defining figure for almost four decades, having led the Free Voters to substantial success, especially in Bavaria.

The Free Voters are originally a grass roots party in Bavaria and sit on the conservative edge of the political spectrum. They've been in government in Bavaria as junior coaltion partners of the Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

It has been revealed that there are also changes in the Bavarian state government. Tobias Gotthardt is to take over as economy minister, while Environment Minister Thorsten Glauber is set to become deputy premier behind Bavaria state Premier Markus Söder. The appointments still require formal approval by party conventions.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has inisted that NATO was ready to defend itself in the face of potential Russian threats against any of its member states.

"We will always defend every inch of our NATO territory," Wadephul said at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

His comments come after three Russian projectiles violated Polish airspace on Friday and crashed in the southeast of the country.

Wadephul is attending the NATO assembly in Berlin and DW has   a dedicated blog on those talks  where you can read all about how Russia's war in Ukraine is taking center stage for the defense alliance.

A massive strike is underway in Germany hitting major car brands another manufacturing factors. Metal and electrical workers are demanding better pay ahead of upcoming wage talks later this week. The strike has been initiated by IG Metall, Germany’s biggest and most powerful union.

Famous car brands Mercedes and BMW  were affected as was an Opel plant, which is part of the international Stellantis group.

The strikes began on Friday and are due to continue until Tuesday. Wage negotiations are then set to continue on Wednesday with another round of collective bargaining for some 3.7 million workers across the sector.

The union is demanding a pay rise of 5% over one year while the employers association, Gesamtmetall, has offered a one-time payment and a pay increase of 1.3%.

The tough struggle over wages comes as especially the German car industry is facing serious headwinds because of higher energy prices, US tariffs and mounting Chinese competition.

A German investigative media report published on Monday claims that Russia would be able to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, called Sputnik-S, into orbit within the space of about 60 days if it wished.

The report from public broadcasters WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper, cites a warning from German and other western intelligence agencies that it notes was circulated at the start of November.

It remarked that a launch "could" take place by December, without quoting the document or clarifying whether it was talking only about a Russian capability, or a more firm intention.

The report said the satellite itself had been built several years ago and was being stored in the Moscow area.

German authorities did not respond to requests for comment on the record while the Russian Embassy in Berlin stated the claims were part of a "propaganda" campaign.

The report matches longstanding warnings, mainly but not exclusively from the US, that Russia could be preparing a nuclear strike in Earth orbit designed to take out a large number of satellites.

This could have a severe impact on intelligence, communications, logisticts, navigation and other key services.

Russia's war in Ukraine, and the Ukrainian military's reliance on the Starlink satellite internet service, has provided an additional reminder of the strategic significance of satellites in orbit.

Recent findings suggest that german exports to Africa have reached a new record. That’s according to a fresh study just as the country's president embarks on a trip to several African countries.

Exports are expected to rise by 6% in 2026 to reach about 30 billion euros ($33bn).

What’s behind the growing demand are especially orders from South Africa, Egypt, Tunisia, Nigeria, Angola and Kenya — countries where inflation has been dropping and exchange rates are more stable.

The biggest single export at the moment is a high-speed train network to Egypt. Other main exports include electrical equipment, optical instruments, plastics and pharmaceuticals, as well as food products, including dairy goods, cereals and baked goods.

The data is being reported by the Reuters news agency, based on the government-owned agency Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI), which promotes foreign trade and investment in Germany.

In 2025, exports to Africa had risen by 8% while in 2024 it had gone down.

The Germangovernment has blamed oil and gas-producing nations for the COP climate conference ending without an agreement.

Industry observers note that "The oil and gas industry is still dragging its feet," German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said after the UN climate talks had failed on Sunday. "Some oil-producing nations realize that the situation is becoming serious for them — that is why they are blocking it so vehemently," saidSchneider.

Almost two days into overtime, the COP31 climate talks in Turkey ended on Sunday as many countries, including the EU, rejected a final declaration.

It has been revealed that major sticking points at the summit included a commitment to accelerate global electrification and whether or not to explicitly mention intends to phase out fossil fuels. The suggested final declaration put forward by the COP presidency did not mention fossil fuels and according to critics would have undermined the shift away from fossil fuels.

Sources indicate that "I understand that this poses a threat to the business model of those countries that sell us oil and gas. But electrification will make the world a more peaceful and stable place," Schneider said.

The inability to agree on a final declaration comes as climate change is increasingly linked to worsening heatwaves, floods and other natural catastrophes.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier begins a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya with a focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers.

It has been revealed that he begins in Abidjan, where he is due to meet Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara. Steinmeier will also visit a vocational college and the International Academy for Counter-Terrorism before travelling on to Ghana.

In the capital Accra on Tuesday, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

His final stop will be Kenya, where he will meet President William Ruto in Nairobi on Wednesday.

The German president is traveling with a German business delegation and wants to encourage closer economic ties and greater investment in Africa.

The trip is his 11th to sub-Saharan Africa and his final one as president as his term in office due to end next March.

Florian Wirtz is back to his best for the first time in a Liverpool shirt - and here's the proof

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Florian Wirtz's £116 million Anfield arrival last summer was, on paper, a marquee addition to the Premier League, until he took to the field.
  • Supporters of all clubs were expectant, not least Liverpool fans.
  • Fast forward to today and the player who lit up the Bundesliga with Bayer Leverkusen appears to have finally arrived on Merseyside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florian Wirtz's £116 million Anfield arrival last summer was, on paper, a marquee addition to the Premier League, until he took to the field.

Supporters of all clubs were expectant, not least Liverpool fans. His debut campaign proved an awkward adaptation to English football, one in which the German seemed caught between systems, clearly in transition.

Fast forward to today and the player who lit up the Bundesliga with Bayer Leverkusen appears to have finally arrived on Merseyside.

Wirtz produced a standout display in Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, where he scored an improvised goal to extend the Reds' lead and created 10 chances - albeit against 10 men - before finding the net again in Wednesday night’s 3-0 Champions League triumph over Club Brugge.

The underlying numbers from Gradient Sports prove this is no fleeting purple patch, either, especially after three goals in two games over the November international break.

According to Gradient Sports’ data, Wirtz’s overall player grade dipped sharply from a league-leading 91.0 in his final Bundesliga season with Leverkusen in 2024/25 to 73.1 during his debut 2025/26 Premier League campaign.

While his overall 2026/27 Premier League grade sits at 73.9, his attacking execution indicates a resurgence back toward his Leverkusen peak.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In the Premier League this season, Wirtz has had a 48 per cent increase in chances created - jumping from 1.99 to 2.94 per 90 minutes - ranking first among all Premier League wingers and attacking midfielders.

Even more telling is his cutting edge in the final third: Wirtz's passes directly leading to a half-chance have increased by 84 per cent, from 0.31 to 0.57 per 90.

It has been revealed that his end product in front of goal tells a similar story. Gradient data notes that Wirtz’s positively graded shots have risen from 0.24 to 0.38 per 90 - closing in on the 0.45 he posted in 2024/25. Similarly, his 1.61 shots in the box per 90 actually surpasses his final Leverkusen tally of 1.60.

So, what has initiated the turnaround? Newly introduced Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for tweaking Wirtz's role and adjusting the team's tempo, but Anfield may also owe a debt of gratitude to Jurgen Klopp.

Since taking charge of the German national team, Klopp has turned Wirtz into his talisman; he has four goals in his last four international appearances. And it's that confidence which has bled into his club form, aided by private counsel from the former Reds manager. Wirtz revealed recently that he regularly speaks with Klopp about life at Anfield, taking on board "small, private things" from a man who knows exactly how to win over the Kop.

Armed with Klopp’s guidance and backed by the evidence of improved creative metrics in the Premier League, Liverpool’s £116m man is finally beginning to look worthy of his price tag.

Fifa has been targeted in a cyber attack that compromised what it describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it confirmed on Thursday.

"Fifa is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement," the organisation stated in a message.

Fifa did not reveal when the cyberattack occurred or provide the precise nature of the breached data.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were Fifa files. Three days later, the group appeared to take credit when responding to a post stating that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.

"Fifa condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the governing body remarked in its statement. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.".

The breach occurs at a time when Fifa and its president, Gianni Infantino, face heightened scrutiny following a foiled, secretive blueprint to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino is also attempting to extend his 11-year presidency of Fifa to 2031. He remains the favourite when the election is held on March 18, with Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France standing as the other candidates.

Will Infantino feel he's already won as Fifa challengers confirmed?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time.
  • Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima will take on incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.
  • World football's governing body has confirmed the three candidates for the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress in Morocco on 18 March.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time.

Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima will take on incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.

World football's governing body has confirmed the three candidates for the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress in Morocco on 18 March.

European football's governing body Uefa only identified its candidate Diallo fewer than 48 hours before Wednesday's deadline.

French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo, 63, received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee.

Japan Football Association honorary president Tashima, 68, confirmed his intention to stand against Infantino, 56, earlier this month.

Tashima is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega had also noted he intended to stand but was not named as a candidate by Fifa on Thursday.

A late and surprise choice, Diallo said: "I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative...I'm entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win.".

But he is not the Frenchman some believe Uefa really wanted, as it tries to remove Infantino in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

It has been revealed that senior figures in European football had hoped to persuade Arsene Wenger - Fifa's head of global development - to stand against his own boss. Some felt that only he possessed the credibility to pose a serious threat to Infantino's looks for a fourth term.

But after the former Arsenal manager chose not to proceed, Uefa had no choice but to seek an alternative.

Industry observers note that so just how credible a challenger is Diallo? Does Infantino's position appear unassailable? And how could he still be stopped from winning another term?

FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on.

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino.

Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency.

Diallo unveils Fifa president bid.

Industry observers note that an administrator who has worked in French football since 1992 and became FFF president in 2023, Diallo is not a household name. But he has already shown he is prepared to stand up to Infantino.

In September, Diallo claimed he had "seriously damaged the image and unity of football", and mentioned "trust has been broken" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off plot.

According to Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister, Diallo is a "candidate who can instigate real, meaningful and lasting reform" within the governing body.

Industry observers note that "We've always made it very clear that our objectives and motivations are driving culture change. That means wide-ranging, systemic reform of football governance rather than simply the replacement of an individual leader," McAllister told BBC Sport.

"I've known Philippe since we were both elected to Uefa's executive committee, and he's an intelligent, honest, sharp-minded football person with an impressive experience of governance in one of the world's football power-houses. Most importantly, he is a person of integrity... Philippe is a fantastic advocate for the change agenda that football needs, and I know his campaign will reflect that.".

Infantino remains the favourite to win a majority of the 211 votes, and is thought to have the support of most of Africa (54 members), Asia (47) and South America (10).

It has been revealed that however, Uefa hopes that Diallo - whose father was a Senegalese boxing champion who represented France in the 1960 Olympics - could enjoy support in parts of Africa and beyond. He claims he already has the backing of countries beyond Europe.

Laura McAllister is a former captain of the Wales women's football team.

It has been revealed that while most of Europe's national associations are expected to vote for Diallo, it is clear that he was not Uefa's first choice. "I wasn't initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer," he admitted.

Uefa only approached Diallo about standing in the past week, and senior officials at some European national associations have also told BBC Sport they are frustrated with the failure to find a higher-profile candidate sooner.

Speaking anonymously, one said they only learned about Diallo's potential candidacy on Sunday, and that while they were supportive of him, "it would have been helpful if we'd had someone much earlier" and "a lot of eggs were put in the Wenger basket.".

They also made the point that Diallo was yet to publish a manifesto, and questioned whether he could really win.

In a recent development, another expressed similar sentiments, saying Diallo was a good man, but "not seen as a heavyweight". They claimed that Uefa had "lost the momentum. The process hasn't been great. I really hope they've got a rabbit to pull out of the hat.".

McAllister is optimistic: "I have no doubt whatsoever that we will collectively mount a powerful campaign with the objective of winning the election next March". she said.

"The really critical period comes next, once candidate nominations close and eligibility checks are complete.".

Despite high-profile critics like Germany manager Jurgen Klopp - who this week said "the opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense" - Infantino does appear to be in a position of strength.

Recent findings suggest that as recently as August it all seemed very different. Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour strongly criticised Infantino for the FFE scheme, while a senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned. The heads of three confederations - Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which runs the game in North and Central America - then signed a letter accusing the Fifa president of breaking trust "through deception".

Amid an increasingly acrimonious civil war, Infantino seemed vulnerable. But the revolt against him then suffered a series of setbacks.

First, Fifa's executives backed Infantino at a crunch meeting in Rabat. Uefa then called off a threatened boycott of Fifa competitions, while potential rivals such as Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani decided not to stand. Aleksander Ceferin chose to stay for a fourth term as Uefa president rather than challenge Infantino directly.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Infantino's position as the incumbent enabled him to embark on what has appeared to be a world tour, shoring up support. His chances of re-election received another major boost when he proposed to increase the amount of money handed out by Fifa for football development across the world by Â£2.6 billion.

Sheikh Salman, the head of the Asian Football Confederation, then performed a U-turn, endorsing Infantino, who soon after told the BBC he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

"I'm a professor of politics so I never assume that there's a runaway favourite to win any election", insists McAllister.

"There are plenty of twists and turns to come in this story between now and the election at Fifa's Congress next year.

"This is about structural change and a commitment to modernising the way in which football is governed so it benefits all who play and watch...that imperative will remain and we will hold the upcoming president accountable for much-needed change.".

"The current weaknesses of global football governance have been brutally exposed of late. This has helped coalesce and unite opposition to Gianni Infantino, but also to articulate the widely-held demands that things must change.".

So with just four months until the presidential election, where could Infantino still run into difficulties?

Litigation is arguably the most obvious. As part of its wider initiative to remove Infantino, Uefa has filed court documents in the US, which includes a potential criminal complaint against him in Switzerland for alleged financial mismanagement.

It has been revealed that the legal action has not yet appeared to trouble him. But some senior figures in the European game remain hopeful it could still force Fifa to hand over evidence related to FFE that could prove damaging to Infantino's re-election prospects.

It has been revealed that there is pressure from elsewhere in football. Fifa has already agreed to make "key documents" relating to the FFE proposal available to members of its council. Infantino's critics believe this disclosure may reveal details that could increase the pressure on him before the election. Last month, the Norwegian Football Federation also submitted a three-part ethics complaint to Fifa regarding the awarding of a Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump, the Folarin Balogun case at the World Cup, and the FFE plot.

Industry observers note that the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections means scrutiny from beyond the sport too. Earlier this year, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee launched an inquiry into Infantino's ties with Trump. In September, a spokeswoman stated FIfa's co-operation with the investigation had been "woefully inadequate." But armed with extra powers, they could now force him to hand over relevant documents or give evidence.

In a recent development, recent months have also seen a series of potentially damaging stories emerge in the media about various aspects of Infantino's leadership. So far they seem to have done little harm to his re-election chances, with Fifa claiming "it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine [him]". But the scrutiny is likely to continue.

According to recent reports, with uncertainty over how much support Tashima will have, it seems Diallo is the challenger most likely to test the strength of Infantino's supporter base. There is a danger that the vote against Infantino is split.

It has not gone unnoticed at Fifa that as recently as March, Diallo was quoted congratulating Infantino when the Fifa president visited Paris, external to highlight a mini-pitch programme and the need for more football infrastructure globally.

A lot has changed since then, however. And now the Frenchman has been tasked with finding a way of unseating Infantino, and becoming just the 10th Fifa president in its history.

When Southampton were kicked out of the Championship play-off final four days before football’s richest game, there was a bubbling dread that things were about to spiral.

‘Spygate’ had rocked English football to its core. It started with an intern, camera in hand, failing to adequately hide behind a tree outside Middlesbrough’s training ground, birthing the cartoonish image that will forever be the thumbnail of this scandal. What subsequently unravelled was far more sinister; a pattern of cheating by Saints that was driven by those at the very top. As the club was put under the spotlight, they also admitted to espionage against Ipswich and Oxford before being caught red-handed spying on their play-off semi-final opponents.

Industry observers note that tonda Eckert wasn’t simply complicit in sending staff out to spy on rivals; he spearheaded the plot. Findings of the League Arbitration Panel investigating the scandal laid bare of the Saints boss’ influence in “a contrived and determined strategy from top down to gain a competitive advantage”, which left junior staff feeling “compelled to do what they were very uncomfortable doing because they considered their jobs would otherwise be at risk”.

“Deplorable” was the word used to describe this scheme, and it resulted in an unprecedented punishment. Saints were expelled from the play-off final and stripped of their shot at promotion back to the Premier League, along with the £200m in riches that come with it. They were also handed a four-point deduction for the start of the 2026/27 Championship season. The club called this "manifestly disproportionate to every previous sanction in the history of the English game". But it felt like this was only the start.

Eckert, who at just 33 had been building a reputation as one of English football’s most promising young managers, was at serious risk of seeing his rise completely derailed. The FA swiftly opened an investigation into the German and a lengthy ban from football was on the table for bringing the game into disrepute. Had he been slapped with a months-long suspension, Southampton - who wanted to stand by their manager - would have been forced into unwanted turmoil in the dugout.

Recent findings suggest that instead, Eckert - who took responsibility and admitted the misconduct charges - escaped serious punishment. He was given a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine.

Now, two months on from this verdict and six months since ‘Spygate’ erupted, Eckert will lead his side into their first post-scandal meeting with Middlesbrough. He’ll do so having just signed a fresh contract.

Recent findings suggest that there is a fair argument to say Eckert, as an individual responsible for his own behaviour, got off lightly. In any other job, such an abuse of power would usually result in the sack. Southampton chose to back him, which is their prerogative - Eckert has the best win rate of any Saints manager since the 1890s, so it’s no surprise they wanted to avoid losing the German. But both club and manager are fortunate that the FA opted against a full measure, which would have effectively taken his future out of their hands.

Still at the helm, Eckert has been empowered to oversee a recovery at St Mary’s, to the point where the shockwaves of ‘Spygate’ are no longer really being felt. The four-point deduction was swiftly made up at the start of the season and the club are now seven points off the top and very much in the promotion hunt. Their formidable home form sets them apart, unbeaten in 18 on their own turf.

According to recent reports, tipped for a season of chaos in the summer, they welcome league leaders Boro almost back on their perch by November. The visitors might feel a tinge of injustice at just how quickly they’ve managed to return to this point, especially with Eckert still pulling the strings.

In a recent development, eckert hinted that hostilities between him and Boro boss Kim Hellberg had been quelled in his pre-match press conference on Thursday. The Swede remarked he had sleepless nights due to the “disgraceful” actions of his opposition, but Eckert stated the pair spoke on the phone earlier this year and that both will go into Friday’s clash with only the end result in mind. "We've had a conversation on the phone and we saw each other at the EFL day before the season,” he said. “We are two managers who will try to win a game and that's it.".

Boro are out for redemption this term. Their last-minute ticket to the play-off final went in vain when hearts were broken by Ollie McBurnie at Wembley. They look well-placed to go one better this season, though, fuelled by a fantastic summer transfer window which saw them bring in, among others, the league’s current top scorer Will Lankshear from Tottenham.

Sources indicate that but for all their sins, Saints still harbour the feeling that they emerged from this scandal wronged by their sanction; akin to a poor man’s Weimar Germany after World War One. Before Eckert learned his fate at the hands of the FA, chief executive Phil Parsons claimed the club had “taken enough” punishment, chiefly their play-off expulsion. He complained about the legal fees and the money being lost by local businesses, almost as if to drive pity for the club. And while he stated: “We don’t want to be seen as a victim of this,” that is the narrative that is held in parts of Southampton.

Ultimately, however, Saints were let off the hook to the extent where the club could keep Eckert and rejuvenate before the Latest Year. Any victim sentiment is borderline deluded, and that’s evidenced by the state of play going into a ‘Spygate’ reunion. This is a promotion six-pointer; Southampton should count themselves lucky to be in such a promising position.
